name: Reba
title: Midianite king
summary: Reba was one of five Midianite kings who were killed by the Israelites after God's command through Moses. He was one of the five kings who ruled over Midian at the time when Israel prepared to enter the Promised Land. His downfall was part of God's judgment against the Midianites for their role in leading Israel into idolatry at Baal-Peor.

keyEvents.title: The War Against Midian
keyEvents.description: God commanded Moses to take vengeance on the Midianites for their role in leading Israel into sin and idolatry at Baal-Peor. An army of 12,000 Israelites was sent out against Midian.

keyEvents.title: Reba's death in battle
keyEvents.description: Reba was killed along with the four other Midianite kings—Evi, Rekem, Tsur, and Hur—during Israel's campaign against Midian.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Balaam
keyEvents.description: In the same battle where Reba was killed, the prophet Balaam was also put to death by the sword. Balaam had been the advisor who suggested using Midianite women to lead Israel into sin.

keyEvents.title: Reba Mentioned Among Sihon's Vassals
keyEvents.description: In the book of Joshua, Reba is listed as one of the Midianite princes who were vassals under the Amorite king Sihon and were killed by the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: Background: Israel's Sin at Baal-Peor
keyEvents.description: Midianite women led Israelite men into idolatry and immorality at Baal-Peor, which provoked God's anger and brought a plague that killed 24,000 Israelites. This was the direct cause of the war against Midian.
